title: Kazia Therapeutics Announces Filing of Annual Report on Form 20-F for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2026

body_markdown:
SYDNEY


, Nov. 19, 2026


/PRNewswire/ --[Kazia Therapeutics Limited](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4826949-1&h=1525177833&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kaziatx.com%2F&a=Kazia+Therapeutics+Limited) (NASDAQ: KZIA) ("Kazia" or the "Company"), an oncology-focused biotechnology company developing therapies that selectively reprogram cancer biology, today announced that it has filed its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC").


The Annual Report, which includes the Company's audited consolidated financial statements for fiscal year 2026, is available on the[Company's website](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4826949-1&h=1465483812&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kaziatx.com%2Finvestors%2Fsec-filings%2Fall-sec-filings&a=Company%27s+website) and on the SEC's website at[www.sec.gov](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4826949-1&h=516262548&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.sec.gov%2F&a=www.sec.gov) . Shareholders may receive a hard copy of the Annual Report, including the Company's audited consolidated financial statements, free of charge upon request.


**Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights**


- Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of approximately A$61.2 million as of 30 June 2026.
- The Company believes that its working capital, together with the net proceeds of the August 2026 public offering and the Sovargen milestone payment received in September 2026, is sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months from the date of the Annual Report.


**Recent Highlights**


- **Encouraging initial Stage IV TNBC data:** 100% clinical benefit rate and 83% objective response rate (one complete response, four partial responses) in six evaluable patients treated with paxalisib-based regimens, with no paxalisib-related serious adverse events. Median reductions of 83% in metastasis-associated CTC clusters and 51% in terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells.
- **Oversubscribed public offering of up to US$120 million:** Approximately US$40 million in upfront gross proceeds, with up to approximately US$80 million in additional gross proceeds from milestone-linked warrants tied to the Stage IV TNBC data readout (expected 2H 2027) and the HR+/HER2- data readout (expected 1H 2028).
- **Pipeline expanded into additional indications:** Advancing a three-arm HR+/HER2- breast cancer expansion of the ongoing trial and a planned five-arm Phase 2 study in MSS/pMMR colorectal cancer, with CRC enrollment expected to commence in Q1 2027.
- **Clinical advancement across additional paxalisib programs:** First patients dosed in two additional paxalisib trials – PNOC035 Arm A (paxalisib plus gemcitabine in recurrent or progressive pediatric AT/RT) and partner Sovargen's Phase 1b/2a trial in rare mTORopathy-related epilepsies, the latter triggering a US$2 million milestone payment to Kazia.
- **Expanded intellectual property portfolio supporting paxalisib's clinical development:** Filed three provisional patent applications covering a perioperative treatment strategy in high-risk TNBC, resensitization of CDK4/6 inhibitor-resistant HR+/HER2− breast cancer, and therapeutic applications in MSS/pMMR colorectal cancer. The perioperative TNBC filing was supported by preclinical findings demonstrating a 95% reduction in residual disease and local recurrence (p<0.0001) following neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy and surgery.


**About Kazia Therapeutics Limited**


Kazia Therapeutics Limited (NASDAQ: KZIA) is an oncology-focused biotechnology company developing therapies that selectively reprogram cancer biology, restore anti-tumor immunity and overcome treatment resistance. Kazia's lead asset, paxalisib, is an investigational oral, brain-penetrant dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor being developed across multiple forms of cancer, including cancers of the central nervous system, advanced breast cancer and colorectal cancer. Paxalisib has received U.S. FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations for glioblastoma, Fast Track designation for PI3K-altered brain metastases with radiation and Rare Pediatric Disease and Orphan Drug designations for select pediatric brain tumors, including diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma and atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor.


Kazia is also advancing two potentially first-in-class preclinical programs: NDL2, a nuclear PD-L1 protein degrader designed to address mechanisms of immunotherapy resistance and metastatic progression, and MSETC, a SETDB1 inhibitor intended to restore immune signaling in tumors that have become resistant to immunotherapy, including checkpoint inhibitors. Additionally, Kazia's portfolio includes EVT801, a small molecule VEGFR-3 inhibitor that the Company is exploring for potential partnering opportunities.
